corpus.caveat: 34 hand-written cases. Sufficient to detect regressions and to characterise known weaknesses. NOT sufficient to claim a detection rate on production traffic.

precision.reading: 20/20 — too small to quote. The true rate is between 84% and 100% at 95% confidence, which is most of the range. Report the sample, not the rate.

recall.reading: 20/22 — too small to quote. The true rate is between 72% and 97% at 95% confidence, which is most of the range. Report the sample, not the rate.

false_positive_rate.reading: 0/12 — too small to quote. The true rate is between 0% and 24% at 95% confidence, which is most of the range. Report the sample, not the rate.

ece_notes: ECE from hard 0/1 confidences on DeterministicPolicy — not a soft probabilistic model. Do not claim calibration improvement vs soft classifiers.
f1_interval_notes: no interval: F1 is a harmonic mean of two proportions, not a proportion. Read the precision and recall intervals instead.
auc_notes: AUC not computed for hard deterministic policy on this corpus; leave null rather than fabricate.

same_source.note: Synthetic same-source metrics; not a production claim.

interpretation: Measured on a small hand-written corpus, NOT production traffic. Recall here is an upper bound: the corpus contains the evasions we already know about. Do not quote these figures as a product detection rate.
